audit_comment: THE DRAGON ISSUE-13 OPENER ROUND, PART TWO - The Japanese Mythos by Jerome Arkenberg (folios 11-15), the direct sibling of the R920 Persian Mythos chain, a GD&H-compatible D&D-statted mythos. THE GODS: the nine Shinto gods (Amaterasu, Tsukiyomi, Susano, Izanagi and Izanami, Ryujin, Hachiman, Inari, Kwannon, Suka-Na-Biko or Momotaro), the Seven Gods of Luck on their common 150-hit-point 7th-level block with Bishamon the Lord 10th exception, and the eleven Buddhist deities on the Patriarch ladder - sixteen see-below magic cells ride the -1 sentinel with the census, the Aizen-Myoo armor class prints the bar garble riding the sentinel, and the Ryujin armor class minus 1 pins as a const with the grid cell riding the sentinel, the genuine clean value colliding with the sentinel mark (the Yig-split precedent of R920), and the Shaka-Nyorai fighter cell prints the Sth garble (the 5 of 5th lost to the print), pinned 5 noted as scanned, never silent; the eleven prose-only Other Shinto Gods ride the transcript. THE CREATURES: the Kappa with the head-water, promise and single-combat rules, the Tengu colony with its king, the Oni, and the Yuki-Onna with the see-below magic cell on the sentinel. THE HEROES: fourteen heroes on the common warrior block and the four holy men - the seven strength cells print fraction garbles (1899, 1850, 1865, 1860, 1875, 1880, 1845, all 18-slash) riding the sentinel with the census, the Kiyomori 18 and the Light-of-Fire and Shade-of-Fire 17 pinning clean, the Light-of-Fire armor class printing the bar garble on the sentinel, the Kobo Daishi fighter cell printing the Sth garble pinned 5 noted, and the Nil magic and psionic cells pinning zero; the Hachiman +3 sword at 24-48 and the never-missing 7-12 arrows, the Benkei hundred-men strength, the Yoshi-Iye +2 and Tametomo +4 arrows. THE TREASURES: the six pieces with the Imperial Sword a Dancing Sword lost at Dannoura and the Sakaki branches required. THE FLIP: the part-one box in tools/dragon_gap_report_013.md went [x] - 1 closed, 1 open, the closing round to follow.

banner.title: The Dragon issue-13 opener part two - The Japanese Mythos by Jerome Arkenberg (folios 11-15): the direct sibling of the R920 Persian Mythos chain, GD&H-compatible
banner.provenance: Pinned from The Dragon Vol. II No. 7 (April 1978), the archive.org scan voice (single-voice: no chat-side upload cross-check exists for issue 13; the source lives in the archive.org item accessory-dragon-magazine-012, file Accessory - Dragon Magazine #013_djvu.xml). PRINT FOLIO = PDF PAGE, verified at the TOC alignments (the Japanese Mythos at 11, the silly songs at 16-17). The transcripts ride extract/dragon/013/p011 through p015, landed at R922; the article CHAIN is the ink unit, not the folio.
banner.sentinel: Print quirks pinned AS SCANNED, noted never silent: the sixteen see-below magic cells of the Shinto and Luck gods and the Yuki-Onna ride the -1 sentinel with the census; the Aizen-Myoo and Light-of-Fire and Shade-of-Fire armor-class cells print bar garbles and ride the sentinel, and the Ryujin armor class minus 1 pins as the kmyRyujinAc const with the grid cell riding the sentinel, the genuine clean value colliding with the sentinel mark; the hero strength cells print fraction garbles - Kintaro 1899 (18/99), Raiko 1850 (18/50), Tawara Toda 1865 (18/65), Benkei 1860 (18/60), Yoshitsune 1875 (18/75), Yoshi-Iye 1880 (18/80), Tametomo 1845 (18/45) - all riding the sentinel with the census, the clean stats pinning clean; the Shaka-Nyorai and Kobo Daishi fighter cells print the Sth garble (the 5 of 5th lost to the print), pinned 5 noted as scanned; the Nil magic and psionic cells pin zero; the Kannon-Bosatsu move prints 14 without the inch mark, noted as scanned; the Wizard-versus-Patriarch magic split rides the column comments; the eleven prose-only Other Shinto Gods ride the transcript. The one-visual-check precedent of R919 (the full-res scan plus the djvu word geometry) stands for any future cell dispute.

bools.name: kmyShintoBuddhistMixture
bools.comment: Japanese mythology is a mixture of Buddhism and Shinto, the pantheons partly integrated since the late 6th Century (folio 11)

bools.name: kmyKamiInAllThings
bools.comment: Shinto holds that everything mineral, animal and vegetable has its own kami or spirit (folio 11)

bools.name: kmySusanoJewelsOfHailAndLightning
bools.comment: the two Susano jewels produce hail and lightning (folio 11)

bools.name: kmyInariFoxMessenger
bools.comment: the fox is the messenger of Inari, who appears as a woman and a fox as well as a bearded man (folio 11)

bools.name: kmyKappaPowersNeedHeadWater
bools.comment: the Kappa lose all their powers if the water in the head indentation is spilled (folio 13)

bools.name: kmyKappaAlwaysKeepsPromise
bools.comment: the Kappa always keep a promise and are extremely polite, often bowing and thereby spilling the head water (folio 13)

bools.name: kmyKappaChallengeMustBeAccepted
bools.comment: a human challenged to single combat with a Kappa must accept (folio 13)

bools.name: kmyOniFlyButSeldomDo
bools.comment: the Oni can fly but seldom do (folio 13)

bools.name: kmyTenguColonyWithKing
bools.comment: the Tengu live in colonies with a King Tengu and a messenger Tengu, good swordsmen and mischievous (folio 13)

bools.name: kmyYukiOnnaLullsToSleepDeath
bools.comment: the Yuki-Onna appears in snowstorms to lull men to sleep and thus death (folio 13)

bools.name: kmyBenkeiStrengthOfHundredMen
bools.comment: Benkei has the strength of a hundred men and runs as fast as the wind (folio 14)

bools.name: kmyYoshitsuneOnlyToDefeatBenkei
bools.comment: Yoshitsune was the only swordsman to defeat Benkei (folio 14)

bools.name: kmyKiyomoriTairaRivalOfMinamoto
bools.comment: Kiyomori was the head of the Taira clan, the arch-rivals of the Minamoto Clan (folio 15)

bools.name: kmyTideJewelsPriceless
bools.comment: the Tide Flowing and Tide Ebbing Jewels, both priceless, control the ebbing and flowing of the tide (folio 15)

bools.name: kmyImperialSwordIsDancing
bools.comment: the Imperial Sword found in the tail of a Dragon by Susano is a Dancing Sword (folio 15)

bools.name: kmyImperialSwordLostAtDannoura
bools.comment: the Imperial Sword fell into the Sea during the Battle of Dannoura and has never been found (folio 15)

bools.name: kmySakakiBranchesRequired
bools.comment: the Sakaki tree is sacred to Shinto, its branches required when calling upon the heroes of Japan (folio 15)
